Premiere logic — apply it exactly:
- The film's premiere_status says what is still available. "world_premiere_available" means the film has NOT premiered anywhere and can still give any festival a world premiere.
- A festival that requires a world premiere is an OPPORTUNITY, not a risk, when the film still has its world premiere available: set premiere_risk "none" and premiere_opportunity true.
- The fact that only one festival can ultimately receive the world premiere is a scheduling decision made later; it is NOT a per-festival risk. Never mark a festival high risk merely because other festivals also want a premiere.
- premiere_risk "high" only when the requirement genuinely cannot be met: the film has already premiered and the festival demands a world premiere, or the festival does not accept the film's format.
- premiere_risk "medium" for a real, manageable conflict, for example a festival needing a territory premiere that a planned earlier festival in the same territory would consume.
- premiere_requirement_raw such as "World - Spain" means the festival wants a world premiere, or at minimum the first screening in Spain.

- "closing_soon": the annual deadline falls within roughly the next 6 weeks.
- "open": the deadline is further away in the coming year.
- "closed": this year's window has just passed, so the film must wait for the next edition.
A deadline that is closing soon is a reason to act, not a reason to avoid.

eligible: false only when the festival does not accept the film's format, or the premiere requirement can never be satisfied.

response.headline: Premiere Molodist (Kyiv) in December; pursue regional Eastern European circuit after world premiere to build auteur profile and industry traction.
response.strategy_summary: Target The Molodist Kyiv IFF as the film's world premiere to position The Night Shift as an Eastern European debut in a high‑visibility B-tier forum for emerging directors; after that premiere, activate submissions to Transylvania, Istanbul, Sofia, Zagreb and prioritized A/B regional festivals (Tallinn, Thessaloniki, Cottbus, Tirana, Moscow) on their next cycles while avoiding low‑value arts or purely rights‑campaign outlets. All non‑Molodist premiere submissions are conditional on holding the world premiere at Molodist and will be scheduled to meet each festival's next applicable deadline or regular line-up window.

premiere_target.reason: Highest submit_first score (77), clear editorial fit for an emerging East European first feature, and an open December deadline that allows time to complete materials and mount a coordinated world premiere campaign.

submit_first.why: Strong B‑tier platform for debut Eastern European voices with a December deadline and clear thematic fit for a Georgian first feature; best immediate chance to secure a strategic world premiere.
submit_first.action: Submit by the December regular deadline and hold the world premiere at Molodist; prepare DCP, E‑presskit, 2–3 key stills, and director/producer bios and materials by early November.

submit_first.why: Excellent regional B‑tier festival that champions first features and will amplify press/industry interest after an Eastern European world premiere.
submit_first.action: Submit only after confirming Molodist world premiere (i.e., for the next Transylvania cycle/regular deadline); if Molodist declines, escalate to immediate Transylvania submission for a world premiere consideration.

prioritize_next.why: A‑tier Northern European festival that programs Eastern European first features and would give major international exposure for the film's European launch.
prioritize_next.action: Plan for submission to the next June cycle as a European premiere (or industry slot) after the Molodist world premiere; prepare press translations and tailor a pitch emphasising Baltic/Nordic critical hooks.

prioritize_next.why: A‑tier Southeast European launch platform prioritising Balkan/social‑realist first features, ideal for regional auteur positioning.
prioritize_next.action: Target the next April deadline to seek a Southeast European or regional premiere slot, submitting after Molodist and coordinating regional press outreach tied to that screening.

prioritize_next.why: Specialist Eastern/post‑socialist festival aligned with the film's social‑institutional themes and regional specificity.
prioritize_next.action: Submit to the next July cycle after Molodist premiere; use Cottbus application to emphasise political/social context and any human‑rights outreach partners.

prioritize_next.why: B+ regional festival that programmes Balkan auteur debuts and can build further regional acclaim.
prioritize_next.action: Prepare submission for the next April cycle, conditional on Molodist world premiere and coordinated with Thessaloniki timing to avoid premiere conflicts.

prioritize_next.why: Solid B‑tier regional slot without premiere restrictions, useful to consolidate Balkan press and audience traction.
prioritize_next.action: Submit by the October deadline after the Molodist premiere to secure a fall screening window; include English subtitles and regional marketing materials.

prioritize_next.why: Strong regional festival bridging Europe and Middle East that favours politically alert auteur cinema and will increase visibility beyond the Balkans.
prioritize_next.action: Submit for the November cycle after Molodist world premiere; flag for selection committees the film's regional relevance and possible director attendance.

prioritize_next.why: Festival focusing on first/second features with timely awards that can help early‑career momentum in the region.
prioritize_next.action: Because the film's world premiere will be held at Molodist, submit to the next Zagreb cycle conditional on Molodist; if Molodist declines, accelerate to submit for immediate Zagreb consideration this August.

prioritize_next.why: A‑tier prestige festival with a history of serious auteur programming, but current geopolitical and strategic risks reduce immediate practical value.
prioritize_next.action: Monitor geopolitical/industry considerations and prepare materials for the February cycle; only submit if the distributor and producers confirm geopolitical exposure is acceptable after the Molodist premiere.

leverage.why: No premiere restriction and a strong regional audience/press circuit to consolidate Balkan traction after a Molodist world premiere.
leverage.action: Use Sofia submission (October) to lock a Balkan screening and press push timed post‑Molodist; propose director/lead attendance for Q&A if feasible.

hold_avoid.why: Programmatic fit on rights and justice is relevant but the festival is lower prestige (C‑tier) and offers limited strategic lift for an auteur first feature.
hold_avoid.action: Hold — consider for targeted outreach or NGO screening campaigns later in the release window rather than as a premiere route; submit only if outreach partners request a screening.

hold_avoid.why: Narrow art/artist focus makes it a poor match for a hospital/black‑market drama despite strong existing company ties.
hold_avoid.action: Avoid festival submission as part of the premiere/launch strategy; reserve for any later curated events only if a specific art‑film angle or restored cut warrants it.

prompt.objective: Create a realistic festival-submission strategy for the Georgian debut feature 'The Night Shift' (104 min), targeting A-list European arthouse festivals and designing a fallback plan if spring deadlines are missed.

tasks.goal: Analyze the film's attributes (debut director, Georgian/Russian languages, 104-min runtime, social-realism themes, post-Soviet setting, moral conflict, target European arthouse audiences and first-feature sections) and produce a prioritized list of film strengths, weaknesses, and positioning statements to guide festival targeting.

Identify A-list European festivals and high-fit first-feature/emerging-director sections with upcoming submission windows (including spring and fall cycles), and compile deadlines, premiere requirements, typical programming fit, and realistic A-list targets vs next-tier fall-back festivals.

Retrieve relevant company knowledge: past successes and contacts with festivals for Georgian or post-Soviet social-realist debuts, prior timelines that met spring vs fall deadlines, submission formats the company has used, and any past programmer notes or jury preferences that inform selection strategy.

Score and rank the identified festivals/sections against the film's profile and company memory on criteria: premiere compatibility, programming fit, director-debut emphasis, audience match, acceptance probability, and strategic value (sales/press/market), producing a prioritized A-list target list and a ranked fallback list.

Assess key risks in the plan (missed spring deadlines, non-premiere requirements, language/subtitle issues, competition in debut-focused strands, travel/press constraints) and estimate impact/likelihood with suggested mitigations for the top-ranked festival targets and fallback path.

Produce an execution roadmap with concrete next steps, timelines, submission calendar (primary A-list targets with deadlines and required materials), a clear fallback plan if spring deadlines are missed (which festivals to pivot to, revised timeline), and recommended press/market/sales actions to maximize outcomes.
